newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Incentive shares rise on ABB share sale.
newsitem.headline: Incentive shares rise on ABB share sale.

text.p: Swedish investment and medical technology group Incentive rose early Thursday after announcing it was selling half of its ABB stake for 12.4 billion crowns to institutions and investment group Investor.
At 0810 GMT Incentive was trading 33 crowns higher at 740 crowns.
Investor was 2.5 crowns lower at 395 and ABB dipped 2.5 to 112 crowns.

Incentive announced the sale after the close of the market on Wednesday. Both Incentive and Investor are part of the massive Wallenberg family industrial empire and the sale was seen as a continuing shake-up in the Wallenberg empire.

Incentive said it had sold 110 million series A shares in ABB AB -- the Swedish parent company of Swiss-Swedish engineer ABB -- corresponding to 11.7 percent of the capital and 15.8 percent of the votes for a capital gain of 9.9 billion crowns.

This was part of an ongoing divestment programme so that Incentive could focus on its medical technology business area. It has just acquired Vivra, the U.S.'s second largest dialysis provider, which will it will integrate into its Gambro unit.
